in: In docs/design/CP_AND_VSX_DISCOVERY_CONTRACT.md, extend the liveness section with the completed negative search: the object database was compared field by field between a device the Product Owner confirmed powered off and a device confirmed live, of the same model, version and role -- 372 first-level fields, of which exactly two differed, and both were the object's own identity fields rather than any state. The per-device configuration directories on the management server hold policy and schema artifacts, not status. The management server's own status command reports its own state and its connected administrator sessions, not gateway state. Record this as three planes searched and all three negative, so the UNKNOWN is evidenced rather than merely declared

Add to the same contract a new numbered signal, obtained from the management server's own connection table rather than from the object database: per device management address, whether the management's monitoring channel is established, is failing to complete, is in transition between two observations, or is absent entirely. Four states, named for what they observe

State precisely what that signal is and is not: it is an observation of the management server's channel to a device, taken from the management server, with zero new network traffic and zero device contact. It is not liveness. The contract's existing prohibition on presenting any signal as up or down applies to it unchanged, and it is carried under its own name with its own meaning

State the sampling rule: the failing-to-complete state is a transient state by nature, so a single observation may catch a healthy device mid-handshake. Two observations separated by an interval are required before the state is reported, and a pair that disagrees is reported as in-transition rather than resolved

Record the measurement that produced it, as counts and shapes only: one management server, one software generation, all domains in one read; a large majority of channels established and a small minority failing; every observation stable across the interval; and the failing set contained every device the Product Owner had independently identified as powered off

Record as an explicit hypothesis, not a finding, that the count of failing channels equalled the count of devices whose collection failed in an earlier run of the existing collector, and state what would confirm or refute it. Identity was not verified because the earlier run's addresses are pseudonymized

State the three implementation constraints the measurement revealed: the connection table contains many rows per address for management servers and cluster addresses, so results are reduced per address and only addresses present in the object database are considered; the port on which the channel is observed is derived from the observed established channels or configured, never hard-coded, because a version-pinned constant is a defect this repository has already measured elsewhere; and a Product Owner statement of record is that in this estate a management server and a gateway always communicate from their own addresses, so address translation does not break the join

In docs/design/DISCOVERY_VS_COLLECTION_PYTHON_KNOW_HOW_AUDIT_2026_09_12.md, add a section recording three defects measured in the existing collector during this session: a hard-coded, version-pinned path to the vendor environment profile that does not exist on the management server measured, so the sourcing silently fails and the script works only because the login shell supplies the environment independently; a positional whitespace parse of the object query output that shifts columns when an object's own address field is empty, which would classify such a device as management-unreachable and skip it, latent today only because the production query does not select those objects; and a bounded retry that was attempted on every failed device in a real run and recovered none of them

In the same audit, record the run-shape measurement: the proportion of that run's wall-clock time spent in timeouts against devices that were not answering, derived from the recorded device counts, timeout values and parallelism

Any real address, object name, domain name, serial, certificate subject or port-to-vendor-semantic claim. Counts, shapes and relationships only
